texts.preamble: Kum. Vedashree P vs Shri Murali on 20 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru. (Scch-18) Dated: This 20th day of April 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.4749/2018
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 2.7.2018 at about 8.45 a.m. the petitioner was crossing the road on Aladamara Road, near Government School, Papareddypalya, Nagarabhavi, Bengaluru, at that time, Suzuki Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-01-EX-3585 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner. Due to the impact, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately she was shifted to Essential hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 7 years, studying in 1st standard. On account of the injuries she is permanently disabled and she lost happiness, physically and mentally. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle. Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, she prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and placed exparte. The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its respective written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act. Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-01-EX-3585 and its Kum. Vedashree P vs Shri Murali on 20 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35270277/ 2 validity. Further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the above said vehicle at the time of accident. Further contended that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner. Further denied the age, studying in 1st standard of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost. 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed: 1. 7. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P13 to Ex.P16. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent has not examined any witness nor marked any documents on its behalf.
texts.arguments: Further he argued that, the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued by denying the manner of the accident as alleged in the petition and contended that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner. Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition as against this respondent. On the other hand, petitioner has proved her case through oral and documentary evidence. 17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 26. At this juncture this Court has relied the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2445 in between Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd.,and another, which reads like thus; Quantum - Injury - Principles of assessment - Assessment of compensation in case of children suffering disability - Apex Court observed that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10 per cent and up to 30 per cent to the whole body, Rs.3,00,000; up to 60 percent, Rs.4,00,000; up to 90 per cent, Rs.5,00,000 and above 90 per cent, it should be Rs.6,00,000; for permanent Kum.
